Convert 3D polygons to a voxel on a template's grid and depth levels

Source: R/vector3d_to_voxel.R
vector3d_to_voxel.Rd

Puts SpatVector3D polygons onto the grid and depth levels of template as a presence SpatVoxel: 1 at every cell and level a polygon covers, NA elsewhere. A polygon covers a cell when it touches it, as in vector3d_to_envelope(), and covers a level when its depth range shares some thickness with the slab of water that level stands for, as in envelope_to_voxel(). The slabs come from the template's depth edges (see depth_bounds()), or from bounds when it has none.

Usage

vector3d_to_voxel(x, template, bounds = c("midpoint", "top"))

Arguments

x

A SpatVector3D of polygons, from as_vector3d() or buffer_3d().

template

A SpatVoxel whose grid, depth levels and depth edges the result uses; its values are ignored. Polygons are projected to its CRS if it isn't WGS84. Longitudes from 0 to 360 work too.

bounds

How to place the edges of the slab each depth level stands for when template carries no depth edges: "midpoint" (default) or "top", as in envelope_to_voxel().

Value

A presence SpatVoxel on the grid, depths and depth edges of template, with layers named presence_depth={value}. Stops with an error if no cell and level would be covered: when the polygons miss the grid, have no thickness, or lie outside the template's levels.

Details

Each level is filled on its own, so where two polygons cover one cell at different depths, the levels between them stay empty: polygons from 0 to 50 m and from 200 to 300 m over the same cell cover the levels in those two ranges and not the ones between. vector3d_to_envelope() gives that cell one range, 0 to 300 m, because an envelope holds one interval per cell. Use this function when the next step works on a voxel's levels, for example to compare the polygons with a SpatVoxel of data; intersect_3d(), intersects_3d() and mask() use it for polygons and a voxel.

Polygons with depth_min equal to depth_max have no thickness and cover nothing. A voxel has no time, so the polygons' time intervals are dropped, with a message when any polygon has one.

See also

vector3d_to_envelope() for one depth range per cell, envelope_to_voxel()

Examples

grid <- terra::rast(nrows = 4, ncols = 4, xmin = 150, xmax = 154,
                    ymin = -24, ymax = -20, crs = "EPSG:4326", nlyrs = 4,
                    vals = 1)
temp <- as_voxel(grid, depths = c(0, 100, 200, 300), varname = "temp")
square <- sf::st_polygon(list(rbind(c(151, -23), c(153, -23), c(153, -21),
                                    c(151, -21), c(151, -23))))
bands <- sf::st_sf(
  top = c(0, 200), bottom = c(50, 300),
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(square, square, crs = 4326)
)
polygons <- as_vector3d(bands, depth_min = "top", depth_max = "bottom")

# The 100 m level (50 to 150 m) lies between the two bands, so it stays
# empty; an envelope would fill it.
terra::values(vector3d_to_voxel(polygons, temp))[6, ]
#>   presence_depth=0 presence_depth=100 presence_depth=200 presence_depth=300 
#>                  1                 NA                  1                  1 
terra::values(envelope_to_voxel(vector3d_to_envelope(polygons, temp),
                                depths(temp)))[6, ]
#>   presence_depth=0 presence_depth=100 presence_depth=200 presence_depth=300 
#>                  1                  1                  1                  1
